title: Dutch Foundations — Part III: Home and Surroundings
summary: Learn to describe where things are, talk about your home and neighborhood, give directions, use transport, and describe everyday surroundings.
intendedLearner: Adult learners who already know basic present tense, de/het, simple adjective use, time expressions, and basic Dutch word order.
coverIdea: A simple illustrated Dutch neighborhood showing an apartment, street, bicycle, bus stop, supermarket, park, and changing weather.

designNotes.scope: Topic vocabulary is introduced only when needed by the lesson. Dedicated vocabulary memorization is outside the scope.
designNotes.continuity: Exercises should reuse grammar from earlier lessons and deliberately prepare structures needed by later lessons.
previousKnowledge: basic inversion after a time expression

children.title: Mijn huis
children.goal: Describe a home, its rooms, and what is present in them.

children.title: Er is en er zijn
children.purpose: Introduce existence before teaching precise location.

blocks.content: Use 'er is' for one thing and 'er zijn' for more than one thing when saying that something exists or is present.

blocks.note: The balcony is being introduced for the first time.
Use 'zijn' because the noun is plural.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Nee, maar er is wel een balkon.

blocks.instruction: Complete each sentence with 'er is' or 'er zijn'.
Translate short descriptions of what a home contains.

children.title: Een huis beschrijven
children.purpose: Combine existing adjective and noun knowledge with the new existential structure.

blocks.content: Combine 'er is/er zijn' with familiar descriptions to give a simple picture of a home.

blocks.sentence: Er is een kleine keuken en er zijn twee grote slaapkamers.
blocks.translation: There is a small kitchen and there are two large bedrooms.
blocks.note: This deliberately recycles adjective endings from an earlier lesson.

blocks.instruction: Read a short apartment listing and answer questions about what the apartment has.

children.title: Waar is het?
children.goal: Describe the location and physical position of objects.
preparesFor: later use of Dutch position verbs

children.title: Waar is het?
children.purpose: Move from saying that something exists to saying where it is.

blocks.content: Use prepositions such as 'op', 'in', 'naast', 'onder', 'voor', 'achter' and 'tussen' to describe location.

blocks.sentence: De tafel staat naast het raam.
blocks.translation: The table is next to the window.
blocks.note: The learner will soon examine why Dutch uses 'staat' here instead of a generic verb meaning 'is'.

children.title: Staan, liggen en zitten
children.purpose: Introduce a characteristic Dutch distinction that will recur throughout later lessons.

blocks.content: Dutch often describes location using 'staan', 'liggen' or 'zitten' instead of simply using 'zijn'. The choice depends on how something is positioned or conceptualized.

blocks.translation: The book is on the table.

blocks.sentence: De melk staat in de koelkast.
blocks.translation: The milk is in the fridge.
blocks.note: Containers and upright objects commonly use 'staan'.

blocks.instruction: Choose between a form of 'staan', 'liggen' and 'zitten'.
Translate location sentences where English uses 'is' but Dutch requires a more specific position verb.
Read a description of a room and reconstruct where its objects are located.

blocks.goal: Describe where objects in a room are located.

children.title: In mijn buurt
children.goal: Talk about places in a neighborhood and understand or give simple directions.

children.title: Wat is er in de buurt?
children.purpose: Transfer 'er is/er zijn' from the home to the neighborhood.

blocks.content: The same structures used to describe a home can describe a street, neighborhood or city.

blocks.sentence: Er is een supermarkt naast het station.
blocks.translation: There is a supermarket next to the station.
blocks.note: This combines Lesson 13 existence with Lesson 14 location.

blocks.instruction: Read a neighborhood description and answer location questions.

children.title: De weg vragen en uitleggen
children.purpose: Introduce simple commands and functional use of 'kunnen'.

blocks.sentence: Ga rechtdoor en sla dan linksaf.
blocks.translation: Go straight ahead and then turn left.
blocks.note: Introduces the imperative and previews separable verbs.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Kunt u mij helpen? Waar is het station?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Ga hier rechtdoor en sla bij het stoplicht rechtsaf.

children.title: Onderweg
children.goal: Talk about transportation, destinations and simple travel plans.

children.title: Instappen, uitstappen en overstappen
children.purpose: Turn the separable verbs encountered in directions into an explicit grammar concept.

blocks.content: Some Dutch verbs contain a prefix that separates from the verb in a main clause.

blocks.sentence: Ik stap bij Amsterdam Centraal uit.
blocks.translation: I get off at Amsterdam Centraal.
blocks.note: 'uitstappen' becomes 'stap ... uit' in this main clause.

blocks.instruction: Complete sentences by placing both parts of a separable verb correctly.
Translate transport sentences containing separable verbs.

children.title: Wat ga je doen?
children.purpose: Introduce 'gaan + infinitive' while preparing the learner for later infinitive-final constructions.

blocks.sentence: Morgen ga ik met de trein naar Utrecht.
blocks.translation: Tomorrow I'm going to Utrecht by train.

blocks.sentence: Ik ga morgen de trein nemen.
blocks.translation: I'm going to take the train tomorrow.
blocks.note: The infinitive moves to the end. This pattern will matter again with modal verbs.

blocks.instruction: Read a short journey plan and answer questions about time, transport, transfers and destination.

blocks.goal: Explain how you are going somewhere.

children.title: Het weer
children.goal: Describe weather, seasons and how weather affects everyday plans.

blocks.note: 'Het' does not refer to a specific object.
Useful exposure to 'worden' without requiring full mastery yet.

children.title: Weer en plannen
children.purpose: Make weather grammar useful by connecting it to travel and plans from the previous lesson.

blocks.sentence: Morgen regent het, dus ik ga met de bus.
blocks.translation: Tomorrow it will rain, so I'm going by bus.
blocks.note: Recycles transport and 'gaan'. 'Dus' gives early exposure to connecting ideas.

blocks.instruction: Compare a weather forecast with someone's plans and determine what they are going to do.

blocks.goal: Describe today's weather and tomorrow's plans.

children.title: Wat trek je aan?
children.goal: Describe clothing and choose what to wear based on situation and weather.

children.title: Deze jas en dat shirt
children.purpose: Consolidate adjective and demonstrative grammar through a concrete topic.

blocks.note: Reviews demonstratives and adjective endings together.

blocks.instruction: Choose the correct demonstrative and adjective form.

children.title: Ik trek mijn jas aan
children.purpose: Reuse separable-verb grammar outside the transport context.

blocks.sentence: Ik trek mijn warme jas aan.
blocks.translation: I put on my warm coat.
blocks.note: Shows that separable verbs are a general grammatical pattern, not transport-specific vocabulary.

blocks.instruction: Translate sentences combining clothing, weather and separable verbs.

children.title: Een dag buitenshuis
children.purpose: Close Part III with a cumulative task rather than an isolated grammar test.

blocks.instruction: Read about someone leaving home, checking the weather, choosing clothes, traveling across town and finding a destination.

blocks.goal: Describe a complete trip from home to a destination, including weather and clothing.
